主要讨论点：用户在使用Linux或类Unix系统时因误操作（如执行`rm -rf`命令）导致数据丢失的风险及应对方法。

不同观点：
• gleenn分享了一次因误用`rm -rf`命令差点删除了重要文件的经历，最终因为一个大文件夹减缓了删除速度而挽救了一些文件，并调侃地建议保留大文件作为"缓冲"以保护数据。
• eitland描述了在工作中由于错误执行`rm -rf /bin`命令而导致系统异常的情况，最终通过从另一台服务器恢复文件避免了大量手动工作。
• inejge指出这类事件频繁发生的原因是Unix系统中root权限的绝对性以及文件系统的无保护性，并提到未来可能通过不可变系统和受限执行环境来解决此问题。
• ryao解释了被删除文件仍可通过进程内存恢复的技术细节，建议使用特定工具如`debugfs`或`zdb`来恢复未链接的文件。
• vessenes回忆了1996年误执行`rm -rf /`后通过FTP从远程计算机恢复数据的经历，并讨论了现代网络环境下的复杂性。
• lloeki分享了同事通过telnet误执行`umount /`导致系统混乱的案例，强调了旧Unix系统的无保护性。
• nasretdinov提到在macOS系统上执行`rm -rf /`因文件系统排序而只删除了部分文件的经历，并指出不同系统间的差异。
• nullorempty简单提及了职业生涯初期因误操作移除了所有文件的执行权限。
• zavec描述了一次尝试通过残留的库文件恢复系统的经历，尽管未成功但认为过程有趣。
• nurple展示了其工作站通过Nix包管理器组织文件结构的输出，避免了传统目录结构下可能出现的问题。
• Dwedit建议在删除`/lib`等关键目录后通过USB启动并重新安装系统，以减少停机时间。
• ofalkaed分享了两次误操作导致数据丢失的经历，强调了小心使用绝对路径的重要性。
• udev4096提到了一个相关GitHub问题链接以供参考。
• conceptme描述了在公司中因误操作`rm -rf /`导致系统异常，并通过迅速关机减少了损失。
• mastax建议使用`chattr +i`命令保护关键文件不被误删。

补充讨论：
- 误操作`rm -rf`命令的普遍性和严重性。
- 不同系统和文件结构在应对误操作时的表现差异。
- 通过技术手段恢复数据的潜力和限制。
- 预防误操作的建议和方法，如使用不可变文件系统和受限执行环境。

43444160.article_content:
Let’s first not talk about why this can happen, but deleting
/lib
,
/usr/lib
, or some other essential runtime files happens quite a lot (as you can see:
here
,
here
,
here
,
and
here
). In this post, I will only discuss what happens when you delete
/lib
on Linux and how to recover from that.
The easy solution for everything is to replace the missing files, but this can be difficult if
/lib
is deleted because we won’t have
ld-linux
, which is needed to run any dynamic executable. When you deleted
/lib
, all non-static executable (such as
ls
,
cat
,
etc
, will output):
No such file or directory
You will also be unable to open any new connection using ssh, or open a new tmux window/pane if you are using tmux. So you can only rely on your current shell built in, and some static executables that you have on the system.
If you have a static
busybox
installed, then it can be your rescue. You can use
wget
from
busybox
to download libraries from a clean system.  For your information: Debian has
busybox
installed by default, but the default is not the static version.
Minimal Debian install
If you are worried that this kind of problem might happen to you in the future: Install the static version of the busybox binary, and confirm that it is the correct version.
Installing static busybox
Bash to the rescue
I assume right now that you don’t have a static busybox, and you don’t even have any static executables (which is the situation in many cases, like in the default install of minimal Debian). My solution for this is to download a static busybox from another machine.
I also assume that you have bash installed (which is the default for most systems).  Bash has a lot of default built-ins that we can use.  There is a
solution from here
that can be used to download a file using only built-in bash functions. Other
solutions on this thread
rely on external command (such as
cat
).  Please note that you need to set the environment  variable
LANG
to
C
; Otherwise, this script will incorrectly handle Unicode bytes.
Of course, we can’t
chmod
the destination file to be executable, so we need to overwrite an existing executable. If you have busybox installed (even if it is the non-static version), you can overwrite this file. At this point, you can start the rescue mission: for example, use
wget
to download fresh
/lib
from another system.
Please note that busybox can’t function with a name that is not a busybox applet name. So if you overwrite for example, the
fmt
binary with
busybox
, then it won’t work (it will say:
applet not found
).  If you don’t have
busybox
, I suggest overwriting
cp
, then you can use
cp
to create a copy of
cp
as
busybox
(which will be executable).
cp to busybox
No bash? printf can help
If you have a more advanced shell (e.g: zsh),
it has TCP modules already built in
. You can easily use
nc
from another machine to send a file to the target machine. Now, let’s assume that you have a very basic shell, for example:
dash
. Most shell  (including dash), has
printf
as built-in, and we can use this to construct binary files.
Most (all?) shell’s built-in
printf
implementation supports
\ooo
where
ooo
is 3 digit octal. First approach is to just convert
busybox
, but this file is quite big (2 megabyte). Copy-pasting  large
printf
commands is tedious and is error-prone. We need a small static binary that can help us.
This
printf
trick will also work for other OS, if you can create a small binary for that OS.
Creating a small ELF for Linux
You can create a very tiny executable if you use assembly directly, but let’s try to do this using C, so it can be portable across different architectures. The smallest useful program that I can think of is just to copy from stdin to stdout, so we can prepare
netcat
on a machine:
cat busybox | nc -v -l -p 10000
and then we can do this from the borked machine:
fdio < /dev/tcp/192.168.1.168/10000 > busybox
The source code can be like this:
#include "unistd.h"
int main()
{
char x;
while (1) {
int c = read(0, &x, 1);
if (c!=0) break;
c = write(1, &x, 1);
if (c!=0) break;
}
return 0;
}
If we try to compile this with standard C library (on AMD64 machine), the result is 776KB.
$ gcc -Os -static fd.c
$ du -hs a.out
768K    a.out
The Linux kernel source code contains
a nolibc implementation that we can use
. Using this compilation option:
gcc -Os -Wl,--build-id=none -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables -fno-ident -s -nostdlib -nodefaultlibs -static -include nolibc.h fd.c -lgcc -o fd
We get a 4536 bytes binary. Quite good. If we add
-z max-page-size=0x04
, we can even get a smaller size.
gcc -Os -Wl,--build-id=none -z max-page-size=0x04 -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables -fno-ident -s -nostdlib -nodefaultlibs -static -include nolibc.h fd.c -lgcc -o fd
It is now 672 bytes. Small enough to transfer. We can convert this using Python.
import sys
with open(sys.argv[1], "rb") as f:
data = f.read()
start = 0
width = 20
targetname = sys.argv[2]
while True:
part = data[start:start+width]
if part=='':
break

data.title: DNA testing firm 23andMe files for bankruptcy to sell itself
data.author: healsdata
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：23andMe公司的治理困境、破产过程及其对用户数据的影响

不同观点：
• cloudbonsai：23andMe的CEO拥有49%的投票权，曾多次试图以不同价格（从8美元到0.4美元每股）将公司私有化，但均被董事会拒绝。由于公司每季度亏损5000万美元，最终进入破产程序。cloudbonsai认为这可能是摆脱公司治理噩梦的机会。

• LarsDu88：引用加州司法部长发布的消费者数据警告，认为这是公司即将倒闭的信号。

• ks2048：尽管存在隐私问题，但23andMe曾提供有趣的基因信息。不过考虑到未来可能的数据滥用风险，决定删除自己的数据。

• alexfromapex：已经下载并删除了自己的数据，担心新的买家会以低价收购用户的基因数据。

• xeromal：希望Ancestry能够收购23andMe，认为Ancestry在不良市场中表现出色且未受影响。

• dhruvrrp：认为CEO试图以极低价格将公司私有化，导致独立董事会辞职。

• cwbriscoe：未曾参与DNA网站，但有亲属上传了家族树信息，询问如何在不创建账户的情况下删除自己的信息。

• hardlyfun：提到曾读过有关这些公司拥有大量个人数据的文章，认为尽管这些数据可能被滥用，但公司破产显示其效率低下，短期内难以实施复杂的阴谋。

• theogravity：已经删除数据，担心破产后数据的新拥有者。

• Mengkudulangsat：询问在美国公司破产后，其资产如何被拍卖出售，以及是否能被完整收购且无债务。

• arjie：后悔未上传基因序列，认为最全面的数据库最终会胜出，并提到参与PGP（个人基因组计划），愿意分享更多信息。

• rendall：引用23andMe的数据页面，说明如果公司被出售，用户数据将根据当前隐私政策保护，除非有新的法律条款。

• JoshTriplett：认为公司破产后用户数据成为待售资产是不幸的消息。

• aaronbrethorst：建议某位亿万富翁收购23andMe并关闭公司，删除所有数据，彻底解决问题。

补充讨论：
- 用户对个人数据隐私和安全的担忧。
- 破产过程中公司资产（包括用户数据）的处理方式。
- 对公司治理问题及CEO行为的批评。
- 不同用户对数据保护和删除的实际操作问题。
- 对未来数据滥用风险的预估和应对策略。

争议焦点：
- CEO试图以极低价格将公司私有化，与董事会及独立董事的冲突。
- 用户数据在公司破产后的安全和隐私保护问题。
- 23andMe的商业模式及其对用户数据的责任。

data.title: You need to know about bootc
data.author: nikodunk
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Bootc这一工具，它能让用户像制作应用程序一样，通过容器创建不可变Linux发行版（如SteamOS、Fedora Silverblue等）。传统Linux发行版依然有其价值，但不可变发行版因其稳定性、易用性逐渐受到关注。Bootc简化了操作系统配置，用户可以通过类似Docker容器的方式定义系统，确保每次启动时都具有一致的环境配置。文中以Nginx服务器配置为例展示了Bootc的简单用法，并提到Universal Blue项目进一步提升了用户体验，使得复杂软件如VSCode、Nvidia驱动等也能轻松配置。Bootc的目标是让Linux桌面系统对普通用户更友好，无需额外手动配置或技术支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“bootc”及其相关概念在Linux桌面环境中的作用和必要性

不同观点：
• [account-5] 认为 bootc 及其相关的操作系统（OSs）与自己关系不大。他们表示不理解为什么要了解 bootc，尤其是因为这些OSs他们从未使用过，甚至只听说过其中一个。这暗示他们对 immutable OS 概念缺乏兴趣或需求，尤其是如果他们不使用相关操作系统。

• [MiiMe19] 部分同意 [account-5] 的观点，但进一步解释了 immutable OS 的优势。他们指出，像 bootc 这样的 immutable 系统可以让系统在启动时更可靠，无需担心过去Linux桌面用户常遇到的问题，例如驱动程序、内核修改或新软件包导致的问题。不过，他们质疑 bootc 作为“又一个不可变发行版”的独特性，认为这种技术对游戏机等特定设备可能更适用，但对于普通Linux桌面环境的影响有限。

补充讨论：
• [MiiMe19] 提到，即便使用像 Debian 这样的传统发行版，只要配置好启动镜像，系统也能可靠启动。这暗示他们认为传统发行版已经能满足稳定启动的需求，bootc 之类的技术并非必不可少。

• 争议的焦点在于 bootc 和 immutable OS 的实际应用价值。一方认为此类技术与己无关或无必要，另一方则认为其有技术优势，但对其能否改变Linux桌面环境持怀疑态度。

• 讨论还涉及到不同用户群体的需求差异，例如普通用户与游戏机用户对操作系统稳定性和易用性的不同要求。

At the risk of sounding like every YouTuber out there who wants you to click the âSubscribeâ button right now, I really believe everyone who cares about Linux should start learning about
Bootc
. When looking at the future of Linux and what that could look like thereâs already
a lot of talk
of immutable distos like SteamOS, Fedora Silverblue, or NixOS being the future.
Starting off let me be clear, traditional distros arenât going anywhere. They have their place and people already know and love them. Businesses rely on them. Yet people arenât using them and weâve been talking about âYear of the Linux Desktopâ for longer than I have been alive. Immutable distros (or âAtomicâ as they now like to be called) have been around for a while as well, but are relatively new in the Linux Desktop space and allow end users to be able a Linux desktop like an appliance. They can turn it on and know it will boot properly without having to worry about things users had to worry about in the past like drivers, kernel mods, or new packages breaking things â the ghosts of Linux Desktop Past. If you want to see what can be possible, look at the Steam Deck.
Alright, you get it by now â atomic distros are cool. What makes them even cooler is how you can make your own atomic distro. Enter Bootc! Bootc allows you to make an OS the same way you make an application, using containers! There is no denying that most applications are shipped today as a Docker container and most developers have some experience with them. Bootc takes this existing developer experience and directly translates it to your OS. Lets look at an example to see how easy it can be:
1
2
3
FROM
quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:41
COPY
nginx.container /usr/share/containers/systemd
COPY
nginx.conf /etc/nginx
Simple, right? This copies a file to run a Nginx container as a
quadlet
and a config into the
/etc
folder. This brings GitOps to my OS. With this whenever my machine starts, whether for the first time or millionth time, its going to be configured to work exactly as expected with no extra work or additional configuration. Day 1/2 configuration with other tools like Ansible or Chef are no longer necessary. Everything together in the same repo.
But that was a simple example for an Nginx server, what about something complex like a Linux desktop with all the software I want like VSCode, OpenRazr, and Nvidia drivers? Look no further than
Universal Blue
. This project is the epitome of âI want everything to work out of the box with no extra workâ. In fact
The Verge
recently published an article saying that one of the Universal Blue projects, Bazzite, was a better experience than SteamOS. High praise! They put a lot of work into streamlining the user experience so anything you could want is just a simple command away and it always âJust Worksâ which is exactly the kind of experience normal non-technical users want. Something I can give to my parents and know theyâll have access to all the applications they need and wonât be able to break. Bootc is the way weâre going to be able to achieve that.
Bootc isnât the only piece to the puzzle and Iâm just scratching the surface with what Bootc can do. There are more pieces like ComposeFS & Systemd-sysext but Bootc is where I think people should start. If you want to see more examples feel free to check out
my repo on GitLab
.

data.author: bpierre
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了JavaScript生态系统向ESM（ECMAScript Modules）单格式迁移的必要性和现状。作者在三年前主张双格式（CJS和ESM）并存以方便迁移，但随着工具和生态系统的演变，如今更倾向于ESM单格式。现代工具如Vite、Nuxt、SvelteKit等已原生支持ESM，简化了开发过程。

文章指出，尽管仍有大量CJS包，但ESM使用率在增长。采用ESM的主要挑战包括互操作性问题和依赖解析，但Node.js的新功能使得ESM包可以与CJS包无缝互操作。双格式维护复杂且容易出错，因此建议新包、浏览器包和独立CLI工具优先考虑ESM单格式。

作者认为，2025年将是ESM广泛采用的重要节点，建议包作者根据用户需求逐步迁移到ESM单格式。高层次框架和工具的支持将推动这一进程。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [graypegg] 认为文章忽略了浏览器对 ESM 的原生支持，如 `<script type="module">` 和 importmaps。他觉得浏览器支持比打包工具的支持更“正式”。
• [jauntywundrkind] 强调 Node.js 对 ESM 的支持，特别是在 Node 22 中的 `require(esm)` 功能及其向后移植到 Node 20，这使得完全放弃 CJS 成为可能。
• [Klaster_1] 分享了在 Node.js 中使用原生 TypeScript 支持的积极体验，认为可擦除语法是未来的发展方向，并期待其在浏览器中的实现。
• [airstrike] 对文章中提到的“工具已准备好”持怀疑态度，指出许多现代工具虽然支持 ESM，但与作者的定义可能不一致，并列举了多个工具的例子来支持这一观点。
• [paulddraper] 认为在生产系统中使用 ESM 的最大障碍是可观察性和追踪工具依赖于 CJS 的 `require()` 功能。
• [ilrwbwrkhv] 提出一个更广泛的观点，认为当前 JavaScript 和 TypeScript 开发者的质量较低，使用这些语言的初创公司将面临挑战，而使用 Rust 或 Python 的开发者可能会胜出。

• 争议的焦点之一是浏览器和 Node.js 对 ESM 的支持程度及其在实际应用中的“正式性”和可行性。
• 另一个争议点是生产系统中可观察性和追踪工具对 CJS 的依赖，这可能阻碍 ESM 的全面采用。

43456966.article_content:
Move on to ESM-only
Feb 5
· 15min
The Toolings are Ready
Modern Tools
Top-Down & Bottom-Up
Requiring ESM in Node.js
The Troubles with Dual Formats
Interop Issues
Dependency Resolution
Package Size
When Should We Move to ESM-only?
New Packages
Browser-targeted Packages
Standalone CLI
Node.js Support
Know Your Consumers
How Far We Are?
Moving Forward
Three years ago, I wrote a post about
shipping ESM & CJS in a single package
, advocating for dual CJS/ESM formats to ease user migration and trying to make the best of both worlds. Back then, I didn’t fully agree with
aggressively shipping ESM-only
, as I considered the ecosystem wasn’t ready, especially since the push was mostly from low-level libraries. Over time, as tools and the ecosystem have evolved, my perspective has gradually shifted towards more and more on adopting ESM-only.
As of 2025, a decade has passed since ESM was first introduced in 2015. Modern tools and libraries have increasingly adopted ESM as the primary module format. According to
WOOORM
’s
script
, the packages that ships ESM on npm in 2021 was
7.8%
, and by the end of 2024, it had reached
25.8%
. Although a significant portion of packages still use CJS, the trend clearly shows a good shift towards ESM.
ESM adoption over time, generated by the
npm-esm-vs-cjs
script. Last updated at 2024-11-27
Here in this post, I’d like to share my thoughts on the current state of the ecosystem and why I believe it’s time to move on to ESM-only.
The Toolings are Ready
#
Modern Tools
#
With the rise of
Vite
as a popular modern frontend build tool, many meta-frameworks like
Nuxt
,
SvelteKit
,
Astro
,
SolidStart
,
Remix
,
Storybook
,
Redwood
, and many others are all built on top of Vite nowadays, that
treating ESM as a first-class citizen
.
As a complement, we have also testing library
Vitest
, which was designed for ESM from the day one with powerful module mocking capability and efficient fine-grain caching support.
CLI tools like
tsx
and
jiti
offer a seamless experience for running TypeScript and ESM code without requiring additional configuration. This simplifies the development process and reduces the overhead associated with setting up a project to use ESM.
Other tools, for example,
ESLint
, in the recent v9.0, introduced a new flat config system that enables native ESM support with
eslint.config.mjs
, even in CJS projects.
Top-Down & Bottom-Up
#
Back in 2021, when
SINDRESORHUS
first started migrating all his packages to ESM-only, for example,
find-up
and
execa
, it was a bold move. I consider this move as a
bottom-up
approach, as the packages that rather low-level and many their dependents are not ready for ESM yet. I was worried that this would force those dependents to stay on the old version of the packages, which might result in the ecosystem being fragmented. (As of today, I actually appreciate that move bringing us quite a lot of high-quality ESM packages, regardless that the process wasn’t super smooth).
It’s way easier for an ESM or Dual formats package to depend on CJS packages, but not the other way around. In terms of smooth adoption, I believe the
top-down
approach is more effective in pushing the ecosystem forward. With the support of high-level frameworks and tools from top-down, it’s no longer a significant obstacle to use ESM-only packages. The remaining challenges in terms of ESM adoption primarily lie with package authors needing to migrate and ship their code in ESM format.
Requiring ESM in Node.js
#
The
capability to
require()
ESM modules
in Node.js,
initiated
by
JOYEECHEUNG
, marks an
incredible milestone
. This feature allows packages to be published as ESM-only while still being consumable by CJS codebases with minimal modifications. It helps avoid the
async infection
(also known as
Red Functions
) introduced by dynamic
import()
ESM, which can be pretty hard, if not impossible in some cases, to migrate and adapt.
This feature was recently
unflagged
and
backported to Node.js v22
(
and soon v20
), which means it should be available to many developers already. Consider the
top-down or bottom-up
metaphor, this feature actually makes it possible to start ESM migration also from
middle-out
, as it allows import chains like
ESM → CJS → ESM → CJS
to work seamlessly.
To solve the interop issue between CJS and ESM in this case,
Node.js also introduced
a new
export { Foo as 'module.exports' }
syntax in ESM to export CJS-compatible exports (by
this PR
). This allows package authors to publish ESM-only packages while still supporting CJS consumers, without even introducing breaking changes (expcet for changing the required Node.js version).
For more details on the progress and discussions around this feature, keep track on
this issue
.
The Troubles with Dual Formats
#
While dual CJS/ESM packages have been a quite helpful transition mechanism, they come with their own set of challenges. Maintaining two separate formats can be cumbersome and error-prone, especially when dealing with complex

data.author: klaussilveira
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了推荐系统中的**BeeFormer**方法，旨在解决冷启动问题，即新物品没有交互数据时推荐困难。传统协同过滤（CF）方法依赖交互数据，而内容过滤（CBF）方法依赖物品属性，如文本描述，但后者可能无法捕捉用户行为模式。BeeFormer通过训练语言模型，结合交互数据学习用户行为模式，并将这些知识迁移到未见过的新物品上，从而提升推荐效果。

文中提供了详细的训练步骤和代码示例，包括数据下载、预处理和模型评估。数据预处理时，仅保留评分4.0以上且至少有5次交互的用户数据。由于原始数据缺少文本描述，研究使用LLM（大规模语言模型）生成物品描述以增强模型训练。实验表明，BeeFormer在推荐性能上取得了显著提升。

beeFormer
This is the official implementation provided with our paper
beeFormer: Bridging the Gap Between Semantic and Interaction Similarity in Recommender Systems
.
main idea of beeFormer
Collaborative filtering (CF) methods can capture patterns from interaction data that are not obvious at first sight. For example, when buying a printer, users can also buy toners, papers, or cables to connect the printer, and collaborative filtering can take such patterns into account. However, in the cold-start recommendation setup, where new items do not have any interaction at all, collaborative filtering methods cannot be used, and recommender systems are forced to use other approaches, like content-based filtering (CBF). The problem with content-based filtering is that it relies on item attributes, such as text descriptions. In our printer example, semantic similarity-trained language models will put other printers closer than accessories that users might be searching for. Our method is training language models to learn these user behavior patterns from interaction data to transfer that knowledge to previously unseen items. Our experiments show that performance benefits from this approach are enormous.
Steps to start training the models:
create virtual environment
python3.10 -m venv beef
and activate it
source beef/bin/activate
clone this repository and navigate to it
cd beeformer
install packages
pip install -r requirements.txt
download the data for movielens: navigate to the
_dataset/ml20m
folder and run
source download_data
download the data for goodbooks: navigate to the
_dataset/goodbooks
folder and run
source download_data
download the data for amazonbooks: navigate to the
_dataset/amazonbooks
folder and run
source download_data && python preprocess.py
in the root folder of the project run the
train.py
, for example like this:
python train.py --seed 42 --scheduler None --lr 1e-5 --epochs 5 --dataset goodbooks --sbert
"
sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2
"
--max_seq_length 384 --batch_size 1024 --max_output 10000 --sbert_batch_size 200 --use_cold_start
true
--save_every_epoch
true
--model_name my_model
Evaluate the results. To reproduce numbers from the paper using our hugginface repository, run for example:
python evaluate_itemsplit.py --seed 42 --dataset goodbooks --sbert beeformer/Llama-goodbooks-mpnet
or
python evaluate_timesplit.py --seed 42 --dataset amazon-books --sbert beeformer/Llama-amazbooks-mpnet
Datasets and preprocessing
Preprocessing information
We consider ratings of 4.0 and higher as an interaction. We only keep the users with at least 5 interactions.
LLM Data augmentations
Since there are no text descriptions in the original data, we manually connect several datasets with the original data and train our models on it. However, this approach has several limitations: texts from different sources have different styles and different lengths, and this might influence the results. 本文介绍了推荐系统中的**BeeFormer**方法，旨在解决冷启动问题，即新物品没有交互数据时推荐困难。传统协同过滤（CF）方法依赖交互数据，而内容过滤（CBF）方法依赖物品属性，如文本描述，但后者可能无法捕捉用户行为模式。BeeFormer通过训练语言模型，结合交互数据学习用户行为模式，并将这些知识迁移到未见过的新物品上，从而提升推荐效果。

文中提供了详细的训练步骤和代码示例，包括数据下载、预处理和模型评估。数据预处理时，仅保留评分4.0以上且至少有5次交互的用户数据。由于原始数据缺少文本描述，研究使用LLM（大规模语言模型）生成物品描述以增强模型训练。实验表明，BeeFormer在推荐性能上取得了显著提升。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：A/B测试在广告研究和营销中的作用及其局限性

不同观点：
• [Ozzie_osman] 认为，A/B测试在广告研究和营销中的用途应区分开来。对于研究者来说，如果希望得出广告A比广告Y更有吸引力的结论，需要因果推断，而这些测试无法提供这种推断。然而，对于营销人员而言，只需了解哪种广告支出更有效率，因此不需要因果推断。因此，这些工具在研究中的使用被质疑，但在营销中仍然有用。

• [gdc3000] 对文章表示关注，并提出是否可以在Qualtrics产品中开发某种审核面板，以帮助发现潜在的平台偏差。例如，进行样本比例不匹配或元数据平衡检查。这表明了对A/B测试中潜在偏差的实际解决方案的探索。

• [charcircuit] 质疑为什么人们期望只测量广告创意的影响，认为平台的定向能力也是测量的一部分。实验的目标应是查看哪种创意最能推动指标变化，这表明了对广告创意和平台定向在测试中综合作用的重视。

补充讨论：
• [Ozzie_osman] 的评论揭示了研究和营销对A/B测试结果的不同需求，指出了测试工具在不同领域应用中的局限性。

• [gdc3000] 提出了技术性解决方案的建议，旨在解决A/B测试中潜在的平台偏差问题，强调了技术工具在提高测试准确性方面的可能性。

• [charcircuit] 强调了平台定向在广告效果测量中的重要性，提出了广告创意和平台定向应综合考虑的观点，指出了测试目标设定的多样性。

争议焦点：
• A/B测试是否能够提供足够的因果推断以支持学术研究，或者其主要价值仅限于营销效率的评估。

• 如何在A/B测试中有效识别和解决平台偏差问题，以提高测试结果的准确性和可靠性。

data.title: Everything I learned from (finally) completing The Artist's Way
data.author: cf100clunk
data.article_summary: 《The Artist's Way》是一本关于创意的自助书籍，由Julia Cameron于1992年出版，帮助许多人解开创意障碍。作者Madeleine Dore分享了她多次尝试完成这本书的经历，最终在五年断断续续的尝试后成功坚持了十二周的课程。通过每天写 Morning Pages 和定期进行 Artist Dates，她发现自己发生了变化，但又似乎没有改变，强调改变是一个不完美、进两步退一步的过程。她学会了向内探索，理解了支持和尝试的重要性，并认识到勇气而非天赋，是成为艺术家的关键。这本书鼓励被创意障碍困扰的人去尝试，并提供了深刻的自我反思机会。

Everything I learned from (finally) completing The Artist’s Way
Words by Madeleine Dore
Maybe you’ve heard people referring to the morning pages or talking about going on an artist date. Maybe you’ve just started reading the first few chapters, or adopted some of its core practices into your daily routine. Maybe you’ve abandoned it halfway through, or dipped in and out, or even completed the entire twelve-week course.
For those not familiar,
The Artist’s Way
is a seminal text for creative unblocking and was published in 1992 by Julia Cameron. It has sold over five million copies and has helped demystify the creative process and transform countless lives, from
philosophers
to
illustrators and authors
.
In many of the hundreds of conversations I’ve had with creatives, I’ve asked or been asked the question, “Have you read
The Artist’s Way
?” The answer that follows is often some iteration of, “I enjoyed some of the exercises, but have never finished the book,” or “it’s been sitting on my shelf for years.”
“
“I’m completely changed, and simultaneously unchanged. That, to me, is the wonderful thing about it ­– change is imperfect, it’s two steps forward and one step back, and often vice versa. When it’s lasting, it’s almost undetectable as your new self and your old self merge and stroll and stumble together.”
”
Five years ago, while on a break after finishing studies I bought the Kindle version and began the week by week tasks with gusto, filling three pages with stream-of-consciousness writing each morning and taking myself on artist dates. By week three it came to an abrupt stop.
It’s difficult to determine why I didn’t keep stumbling through – perhaps it was feeling daunted by the “homework” or the religious undertones that didn’t resonate. In the proceeding years, I would stop and start the habit of the morning pages, what Julia Cameron describes as the ‘primary tool for creative recovery’.
With a particularly rocky start to the year, I had decided to be more diligent with filling three pages of brain drain each morning, but hadn’t yet picked up the text I put down five years ago. It wasn’t until an afternoon spent reading by the pool with a dear friend that I spotted her copy of
The Artist’s Way
and began to flip through the pages again. Snippets like “get out of the way, let it work through you” and “you have to stop telling yourself it’s too late” were a balm for this particular period of stuckness I was experiencing.
It was time. I moved into a new sublet in Melbourne and with the new environment came a clean slate to create new habits. I found a copy in a second-hand bookstore, the owner tapping on the cover saying “now this, this will change your life” while she put it through the cash register. Later that evening, I began from the beginning, the homework now viewed as a bedrock for a new routine, and the religious undertones swapped out for words like ‘flow’ and ‘energy’.
Twelve weeks, a dozen artist dates and three Moleksine journals filled with morning pages later, I closed the final page of
The Artist’s Way
and find myself in New York City.
I’m completely changed, and simultaneously unchanged. That, to me, is the wonderful thing about it ­– change is imperfect, it’s two steps forward and one step back, and often vice versa. When it's lasting, it's almost undetectable as your new self and your old self merge and stroll and stumble together.
I learned what can only be learned through going inward, even if that means
looking like you’re doing nothing
from the outside.
Here are my week by week notes and learnings – from listening to yourself to reframing lost opportunities – from the book I encourage any individual feeling blocked to dip into.
Lessons from making it all the way through The Artist’s Way
Week 1: Progress not perfection
The first time I began
The Artist’s Way
it helped spark the idea for my labour of love, Extraordinary Routines. This second attempt is exactly five year’s after the first interview was published in 2014.
So many of this week’s lessons resonate with what I’ve unearthed in the conversations I’ve had with creatives and own personal principles – creativity’s chief need is support and the key is to keep trying and experimenting.
I’m stuck by the description of ‘shadow artists’ – those that are drawn to other artists, but are blocked artists themselves and “caught between the dream of action and the feature of failure.”
I’ve spent been five years of inspecting how other people are creative and yet I haven’t written that book I wanted to write, or launched that podcast I wanted to launch. I can’t linger on that point for too long without spiralling.
“Very often audacity, not talent, makes one person an artist and another a shadow artist – hiding in the shadows, afraid to step out and expose the dream to the light, fearful that it will disintegrate to the torch.

data.author: necubi
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Arroyo团队如何通过arrow-rs库实现高效的列式JSON解码。JSON是流处理管道中常用的序列化格式，但其解析过程往往占用大量CPU资源。为了提高性能，Arroyo使用基于Apache Arrow的列式内存格式，并扩展arrow-json以支持流式处理、原始JSON存储和无效数据处理。通过批量解码，Arroyo能将JSON文档转换为列数组，实现高效操作。与Flink使用的Jackson反序列化器相比，arrow-json在处理大型嵌套记录时速度提升了2.3倍。文章详细介绍了列构建、字符串和列表处理以及结构解码等技术细节，展示了如何通过优化JSON解码提升流处理引擎的速度。

43454238.article_content:
Blog
Updates from the Arroyo team
Fast columnar JSON decoding with arrow-rs
February 25, 2025
JSON is the most common serialization format used in streaming pipelines, so it pays to be able to deserialize it fast. This post covers in detail how the arrow-json library works to perform very efficient columnar JSON decoding, and the additions we've made for streaming use cases.
Micah Wylde
CEO of Arroyo
My day job is working on the
Arroyo
stream processing engine, which executes complex, stateful queries over
high-scale streams of events. Computing things like windowed aggregates, stream
joins, and incrementally-computed SQL involves, as you might imagine, a lot of
sophisticated algorithms and systems. Doing it much faster than existing systems
like Apache Flink took careful performance engineering at every level of the
stack.
But…I'm going to let you in on a little secret. The sad truth of this industry,
which no one will tell you, is that so, so many data pipelines spend the bulk of their
CPU time…deserializing JSON
1
.
That's right. Everybody's favorite human-readable and sorta-human-writable data
interchange format has been responsible for >50% of CPU usage on several
high-scale Flink pipelines I've worked on. And so if you want to build a
fast stream processing engine, you need to start with a fast JSON
deserialization strategy
2
.
Arroyo's internal data representation is built on top of
Arrow
, a columnar in-memory format designed for
fast analytical processing
3
. So our challenge is to take row-oriented JSON;
parse it, and build out columns from the corresponding field in each
document. And do this as fast as possible.
Fortunately, we don't have to start from scratch: the
arrow-rs project
includes a very fast JSON
decoder, largely written by
Raphael Taylor-Davies
. I found the approach quite
interesting and thought it was worth writing up. So we'll dig into how
arrow-json works and then talk through Arroyo's extensions to support
raw
JSON
—leaving parts of the JSON serialized—and the ability to skip records in a
batch that don't match the schema. Along the way you should pick up some
intuition for how to work with columnar data, which many engineers find
challenging and unfamiliar in our typically row-oriented world.
Table of contents
But is this fast?
Batched decoding
Stealing from the best
Run the tape
Strings
Lists
An example
Column building
Struct decoding
Primitive and String decoding
Streaming extensions
Raw JSON
Invalid data handling
Wrapping up
But is this fast?
Before we get into the details, we might want to answer the question…is this
actually fast? And the answer is: yes! Benchmarking against the Jackson-based
deserializer used for Flink SQL, arrow-json is up to 2.3x faster:
Benchmark
Java (µs/record)
Rust (µs/record)
Speedup

(See
https://github.com/ArroyoSystems/json-benchmarks
for the benchmark source code and test documents.)
Arrow-json does particularly well with large, deeply nested records, and poorly
with enum-like structures where there are many null fields.
Batched decoding
Arrow, like other columnar formats, operates in
batches
. We're almost never
dealing with just one record (or “row”) of data, because columnar formats
achieve their high performance by storing many values together in a single
array. If you just have one row, the columnar overhead eats any performance
gains.
So our goal is to take a bunch of JSON documents (generally with a top-level
object) and turn them into a set of arrays representing each column of the
schema.
To make this concrete, let's take data representing HTTP server logs:

data.article_summary: 2025年3月18日，由Firefly Aerospace和NASA发布的私营月球登陆器Blue Ghost在月球上拍摄了首批高清日落照片，展示了地球和金星。这些照片是在Blue Ghost于3月2日登陆后、于周末失去动力前拍摄的。Blue Ghost是首个成功垂直着陆并完成全部任务的私营航天器，在月球夜间仍继续工作了五个小时，直至因缺乏太阳能而停止运行。NASA表示，这些高分辨率照片将用于深入分析月球地平线辉光是否由悬浮尘埃造成。尽管所有任务目标已达成，但登陆器钻机仅钻入月球表面1米，未达预期3米。Firefly计划于4月初尝试重新激活Blue Ghost，但工程师对此持怀疑态度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：从月球上看地球日食的照片，以及月球探测器在寒冷夜晚失效的原因。

不同观点：
• [perihelions] 分享了从月球上看到地球日食的照片链接，展示了多个照片。
• [crazygringo] 对这些照片表示困惑，特别是对其中一些照片中出现两个“太阳”的现象提出疑问，怀疑其中一个是镜头光晕或曝光问题，因为从照片上看是地球的暗面。
  • 具体论据：指出其中一张照片中，地球的暗面不应该有过曝的亮光，且另一张照片中，地球似乎遮挡了第二个“太阳”的一部分，这增加了其困惑。

• [celeritascelery] 则关注月球探测器在月夜中失效的原因，特别提到是否是由于电池问题，并推测电路系统应该不受影响。
  • 具体论据：提出电池可能是探测器在寒冷夜晚失效的主要原因，暗示电路系统可能比电池更耐寒。

补充讨论：
• [babyent] 表达了对月球探测器的同情，尽管探测器只是一个机器，但其失效仍然引发了情感共鸣。
  • 这一评论并未涉及技术讨论，而是从情感层面回应了探测器失效的问题。

争议焦点：
• [crazygringo] 对照片中两个“太阳”现象的真实原因表示不解，并提出了镜头光晕的可能性，但未得到明确解答，显示出对照片真实性的争议。

总结：讨论主要围绕月球上看到地球日食的照片真实性及其可能的解释，以及月球探测器在月夜中失效的技术原因。

Blue Ghost lander captures stunning sunset shots on the moon before falling silent
by Marcia Dunn
This image provided by NASA/Firefly Aerospace, Tuesday, March 18, 2025, shows the sun setting on the moon, with Earth and Venus in the distance. Credit: NASA/Firefly Aerospace via AP
A
private lunar lander
has captured the first high-definition sunset pictures from the moon.
Firefly Aerospace and NASA released the stunning photos Tuesday, taken before the
Blue Ghost lander
fell silent over the weekend. One shot included Venus in the distance.
Firefly's Blue Ghost landed on the
moon
on March 2, the
first private spacecraft
to touch down upright and perform its entire mission. It kept taking pictures and collecting science data five hours into the lunar night before it died for lack of solar energy.
This image provided by NASA/Firefly Aerospace shows the sun about to emerge from totality behind Earth. Credit: NASA/Firefly Aerospace via AP
This image provided by NASA/Firefly Aerospace, Tuesday, March 18, 2025, shows the sun setting on the moon, with Earth and Venus in the distance. Credit: NASA/Firefly Aerospace via AP
This image provided by NASA/Firefly Aerospace shows Earth captured by Blue Ghost shortly after landing from the lunar surface. Credit: NASA/Firefly Aerospace via AP
NASA's Joel Kearns said Blue Ghost's series of sunset shots are the first
high-resolution images
from Earth's neighbor. Scientists will need to analyze them in depth, he noted, before making any determination about the horizon glow captured in at least one of the photos and whether it was created by levitating dust. That theory was put forth more than a half-century ago by Apollo 17's Gene Cernan, the last astronaut to walk on the moon.
"What we've got is a really beautiful, aesthetic image showing some really unusual features," Kearns said at a news conference.
Blue Ghost carried 10 experiments for NASA under the space agency's commercial lunar delivery program. While all objectives were met, officials said, the on-board drill could only penetrate 3 feet (1 meter) into the moon versus the 10 feet (3 meters) that had been planned.
Firefly said it will try to activate the lunar lander in early April following the two-week, bitter cold lunar night, although engineers are doubtful it will crank back up.

data.title: Monster Cables picked the wrong guy to threaten (2008)
data.author: wallflower
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了高端音频线制造商Monster Cables向Blue Jeans Cable发出停止侵权函，但Blue Jeans Cable的总裁Kurt Denke是一位有丰富诉讼经验的前律师，强硬回应了这封函件。Denke要求对方提供详细证据，并表明只有在确认侵权的情况下才会采取行动。他强调自己不会妥协，尤其是面对无依据的威胁时，宁愿花费巨资打官司也不接受无理的和解。他还警告Monster Cables不要期望通过威胁来达成快速和解，表示如果诉诸法律，他会全力在法庭上捍卫自己的立场。本文还提到这种强硬态度可能带来的商业宣传效应。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Monster Cable公司的产品、市场策略及相关法律争议

不同观点：
• 一些用户讨论了Monster Cable的营销策略，尤其是其声称的高质量和终身保修政策。例如，[jaredandrews]提到他认识的人因为终身保修而购买Monster Cable，并且多次免费更换。然而，这一政策在2018年左右被取消，现在Monster更多地是通过授权品牌盈利。
• [tqi]和[m463]质疑Monster Cable的音质和价格，指出数字信号传输中电缆对音质的影响微乎其微，且更便宜的电缆也能达到相同效果。
• [npunt]分享了自己在购买音响设备时抵制了Monster Cable的推销，选择了相对便宜的电缆，并成功说服了销售人员。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论提到了Monster Cable涉及的法律争议。例如，[spacedcowboy]和[RustyRussell]引用了Arkell vs Pressdram的案例，以幽默的方式讨论了法律威胁。[ocdtrekkie]则关注了文章作者的背景，对其被解雇的原因感到好奇。
• [biglyburrito]提供了关于Monster Cable和Blue Jeans Cable之间法律纠纷的详细链接，而[stego-tech]表示支持Blue Jeans Cable的法律斗争，并赞赏其不妥协的态度。
• [schumpeter]和[seanhunter]进一步讨论了其他公司涉及商标侵权和法律威胁的案例，反映了企业界普遍存在的商标争议问题。
• [fmajid]高度评价了Blue Jeans Cable，认为其在音响市场中是理性且有能力的选择，与其他夸大宣传的产品形成对比。

争议焦点：
• Monster Cable是否通过夸大音质和质量来推销其高价电缆，以及其市场策略和法律行动的合理性。
• 企业间商标和法律纠纷的频繁发生及其对市场的影响。

Monster Cables picked the wrong guy to threaten
by
Dell C. "D. C." Toedt III
on
2008-04-16
Monster Cables, which makes extremely high-priced stereo cables, has apparently sent a
cease-and-desist letter
to
Blue Jeans Cable
, alleging various kinds of infringement.  Bad move – the president of Blue Jeans Cable, Kurt Denke, is a former litigator who
responded pretty forcefully
:
… Once I have received the above materials and explanations from you, I will undertake to analyze this information and let you know whether we are willing to accede to any of the demands made in your letter.
If my analysis shows that there is any reasonable likelihood that we have infringed in any way any of Monster Cable’s intellectual property rights, we will of course take any and all action necessary to resolve the situation.
If I do not hear from you within the next fourteen days, or if I do hear from you but do not receive
all of the information requested above, I will assume that you have abandoned these claims and closed your file.
As for your requests for information, or for action, directed to me: I would remind you that it is you, not I, who are making claims; and it is you, not I, who must substantiate those claims.  You have not done so.
I have seen Monster Cable take untenable IP positions in various different scenarios in the past, and am generally familiar with what seems to be Monster Cable’s
modus operandi in these matters.  I therefore think that it is important that, before closing, I make you aware of a few points.
After graduating from the University of Pennsylvania Law School in 1985, I spent nineteen years in litigation practice, with a focus upon federal litigation involving large damages and complex issues.  My first seven years were spent primarily on the defense side, where
I developed an intense frustration with insurance carriers who would settle meritless claims for nuisance value when the better long-term view would have been to fight against vexatious litigation as a matter of principle.
In plaintiffs’ practice, likewise, I was always a strong advocate of standing upon principle and taking cases all the way to judgment, even when substantial offers of settlement were on the table.  I am “uncompromising” in the most literal sense of the word.  If Monster Cable proceeds with litigation against me I will pursue the same merits-driven approach; I do not compromise with bullies and
I would rather spend fifty thousand dollars on defense than give you a dollar of unmerited settlement funds.
As for signing a licensing agreement for intellectual property which I have not infringed: that will not happen, under any circumstances, whether it makes economic sense or not.
I say this because my observation has been that Monster Cable typically operates in a hit-and-run fashion.  Your client threatens litigation, expecting the victim to panic and plead for mercy; and what follows is a quickie negotiation session that ends with payment and a licensing agreement.  Your client then uses this collection of licensing agreements to convince others under similar threat to accede to its demands.  Let me be clear about this:
there are only two ways for you to get anything out of me.  You will either need to (1) convince me that I have infringed, or (2) obtain a final judgment to that effect from a court of competent jurisdiction.
It may be that my inability to see the pragmatic value of settling frivolous claims is a deep character flaw, and I am sure a few of the insurance carriers for whom I have done work have seen it that way; but it is how I have done business for the last quarter-century and you are not going to change my mind.  If you sue me, the case will go to judgment, and I will hold the court’s attention upon the merits of your claims–or, to speak more precisely, the absence of merit from your claims–from start to finish.
Not only am I unintimidated by litigation; I sometimes rather miss it.
(Emphasis added; hat tip: Jeff Nolan at
Venture Chronicles
.)
I can relate to Denke’s final comment quoted above ….  I wonder what the attendant publicity is doing for his sales.

data.title: Show HN: GoRead – Terminal epub reader
data.author: Ray-D-Song
data.article_summary: GoRead 是一个用 Golang 编写的命令行 EPUB 阅读器，支持 EPUB3（不含音频），具有跨平台特性。它可以记住最后阅读的文件和阅读状态，支持代码高亮、调整文本宽度、适应终端大小变化，以及查看图片（使用系统默认图片查看器）。此外，它提供 Vim 风格的键绑定，支持暗色和亮色主题。未来计划支持 mobi 格式。用户可以通过命令读取历史文件、导出 EPUB 内容以及使用多种键绑定进行导航和操作。该项目依赖于 Go 1.16 及以上版本、tcell 和 tview 库，并提供了构建多平台可执行文件的 Makefile 脚本。许可证为 MIT。

Remembers last read file (just run

43452892.article_summary: GoRead 是一个用 Golang 编写的命令行 EPUB 阅读器，支持 EPUB3（不含音频），具有跨平台特性。它可以记住最后阅读的文件和阅读状态，支持代码高亮、调整文本宽度、适应终端大小变化，以及查看图片（使用系统默认图片查看器）。此外，它提供 Vim 风格的键绑定，支持暗色和亮色主题。未来计划支持 mobi 格式。用户可以通过命令读取历史文件、导出 EPUB 内容以及使用多种键绑定进行导航和操作。该项目依赖于 Go 1.16 及以上版本、tcell 和 tview 库，并提供了构建多平台可执行文件的 Makefile 脚本。许可证为 MIT。

FaceStream
This is a web app that let's you swap your face in real-time without having a powerful
machine. You can try it out live
here
.
See the gif below for a demo:
Motivation
I discovered the
Deep Live Cam
project and tried to run it on my M1 MacBook, but only got 0.5 FPS. So I wanted to explore how fast and at what latency you could get this to run on a remote server via WebRTC.
How to run this yourself
Prerequisites
To run this yourself you wil need:
uv
A
modal
account as well configured credentials
Then you can run the following command to start the server:
uv run modal serve facestream.main
Or this command to deploy it:
uv run modal deploy facestream.main
Optional: TURN Server for Cellular Networks
On most cellular networks you need a TURN server for WebRTC to work. You can create a TURN app on
Cloudflare
. To use those with this app you need to:
Create a secret called
facestream
in modal with the following values:
TURN_TOKEN_ID=your-turn-token-id
TURN_API_TOKEN=your-turn-api-token
Comment out the following line in
src/facestream/main.py
:
...
secrets=[
modal.Secret.from_name(
"facestream",
required_keys=[SECRET_KEY_TURN_TOKEN_ID, SECRET_KEY_TURN_API_TOKEN],
)
]
...
Credits
This project was inspired by and uses the model of
Deep Live Cam
. Go check out their project. They have some extra features that I didn't implement here. Note that the model used in that project (and therefore also this one) is only for non-commercial use.
Modal
made this easy to build and deploy. They are generously providing free credits to host the live demo.

主要讨论点：关于社交媒体平台上内容审核和言论自由的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持内容审核的观点**：
  - 认为社交媒体平台作为私人企业，有权对其平台上的内容进行审核和管理。
  - 强调平台需要对仇恨言论、虚假信息以及其他有害内容进行控制，以维护健康的讨论环境。
  - 举例说明一些极端言论如果不受限制，可能导致现实中的暴力和冲突。
  
• **反对内容审核的观点**：
  - 认为内容审核侵犯了用户的言论自由，尤其是在政治观点上的审查，可能导致偏见和不公正。
  - 担心平台审核机制缺乏透明度，容易被用作打压不同意见的工具。
  - 引用了一些被错误标记或删除的内容案例，质疑审核的准确性和公正性。

• **中立/调和的观点**：
  - 认为可以在保护言论自由和维护平台健康环境之间找到平衡。
  - 建议建立独立的审核机构或申诉机制，以确保审核的公正性和透明度。
  - 提出通过技术手段，如人工智能辅助审核，来提高审核效率和准确性。

补充讨论：
- **争议的焦点**：
  - 言论自由的界限以及如何在不同文化和政治背景下定义有害内容。
  - 平台审核机制的透明度和问责制，以及如何确保审核标准的一致性和公正性。
  - 用户对平台审核政策和执行的信任问题，以及如何有效申诉和纠正错误审核。

- **其他值得注意的讨论点**：
  - 一些评论者提到了法律和监管的作用，建议政府和相关机构应参与制定审核标准。
  - 提到了用户自我管理的重要性，鼓励用户通过举报机制参与内容管理。
  - 探讨了审核对平台商业模式的影响，以及如何在商业利益和公共利益之间取得平衡。
